correctness.rationale: For x=(a,ξ), y=(b,η), fixed edge-target bracket is det(w_u,w_v) for vertex columns w_v=(a_v,b_v). With U exactly the set of nonzero columns, nonzero target edges B force W(B)⊆U. Since G[U] is a forest, each root has q²−1 possibilities; a prescribed zero edge has q−1 nonzero child solutions and a nonzero prescribed edge has q child solutions. Choices are independent and central entries contribute q^(2|E|), proving exactly q^(2m+|B|)∑_{U⊇W(B)}(q²−1)^c(U)(q−1)^(e(U)−|B|), for every finite forest and q including characteristic 2 and empty graph. All terms nonnegative and U=V is positive, giving surjectivity. Independent direct determinant enumeration checked 103 finite target/forest/field instances; the unrestricted proof is tree rooting.

originality.rationale: Rossmann 2022 studies graphical group conjugacy class sizes, equivalently zero-commutator counts and adjoint ranks. Tittmann–Averbouch–Makowsky provide induced-component polynomials relevant to z=0. Neither measured invariant determines the exact fiber over each nonzero prescribed central target. Resultary's 2026 tree graphical group character-degree polynomial involves weighted support matching numbers (different statistic); its Kronecker path algebra commutator formula uses different multiplication. Prescribed support-by-support full bracket fibers appear best-of-knowledge not covered.

value.rationale: The graphical two-step nilpotent Lie algebra is a standard graph construction and bracket word maps are natural to centralizer and probability questions. An all-target exact fiber law for arbitrary forests and fields is a complete structural enumeration, including shape-sensitive examples where edge-support position changes the answer. It extends genuinely beyond the familiar zero bracket polynomial and can support probabilistic commutator computations.
